books.title: Notes on Stonework
books.text:
Notes on Stonework, from the quarry masons.

Good wall stone splits along its grain, so read the grain before you strike. Set the largest stones at the base with their flat face down, and fill the gaps with chips and packed earth. A wall laid dry will outlast one laid in haste with mortar, provided the footing is deep and the drainage is kept clear.

Masons mark their courses with a cord pulled tight between two pegs. Check the level at every third course and again at the top, since a small error at the bottom grows with every stone laid above it. Rest the work in rain; wet stone is slippery and unforgiving.
